name: Windows — Kernel Driver (.sys) Created in a System Directory
description:
Attacker objective
Load malicious kernel code or a vulnerable driver (bring-your-own-vulnerable-driver) to gain kernel-level control, disable security tooling, or hide activity (rootkit).

Attack logic
Kernel drivers (.sys) placed in the system drivers directory can execute in kernel mode. Attackers drop a malicious or known-vulnerable driver there as a precursor to loading it. New driver files in this location are rare and high-risk.

Why this detection works
File-integrity monitoring records the creation of .sys files in the drivers directory, surfacing driver drops at the filesystem level even without process context.

False positives
Legitimate driver installation via Windows Update, an OEM/hardware driver package, or a software installer.

Tuning
Allowlist verified driver-deployment/patch processes; correlate with driver-load events and signature status; prioritise unsigned or unexpected driver names.

Required telemetry
File Integrity Monitoring (fim.event): file.path (drivers directory), file.extension, event.action, file.hash, host.name.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. file.name/file.hash identify the driver and host.name the system; check the hash reputation and signature.
2. Confirm whether the driver came from a legitimate update/installer; an unknown or unsigned driver is high-risk (BYOVD/rootkit).
3. Correlate the hash with Kaspersky/Defender and hunt for the driver being loaded.
false_positives: Legitimate driver installation via Windows Update, an OEM/hardware driver package, or a software installer.
query: event.dataset:"fim.event" and event.action:"created" and file.extension:("sys" or "SYS") and file.path:*drivers*
